mainTopic: Washing from the כיור: which vessels and which water are valid, and how its rules compare to a מקוה and a רביעית
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא that lets a כהן wash from any כלי שרת, even a tiny one. That seems to clash with the rule that the כיור must hold water for four כהנים. רב אדא בר אחא explains that the small vessel is set into a hole drilled in the כיור. The גמרא then works out which vessels count. The word 'ירחצו' includes a כלי שרת, and the word 'ממנו' excludes a כלי חול, after אביי's קל וחומר from the כיור's base is knocked down. A כלי שרת is the one included because it was anointed like the כיור. Next, ריש לקיש rules that whatever may complete a מקוה may complete the כיור, but not a רביעית. רב פפא explains that this means adding a סאה of other liquid and then removing a סאה. רב פפא also allows immersing small items in a רביעית-sized hole drilled in a מקוה's wall. Finally, ריש לקיש says מקוה water is fit for the כיור, and the גמרא begins testing whether כיור water must be מים חיים; that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא says even a vessel without a רביעית can be used
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא. It says a כהן may wash from any vessel, even one that holds less than a רביעית, as long as it is a כלי שרת. This seems to clash with the rule that the כיור needs enough water for four כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: …or even if they do not hold a quarter-log, as long as they are service vessels!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that it brought as a challenge. The ברייתא says a כהן may wash from any כלי שרת, even a tiny one that holds less than a רביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule under discussion is that the כיור must hold enough water for four כהנים. But this ברייתא seems to say that size does not matter at all; only being a כלי שרת matters. So the ברייתא seems to argue against the size rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of a לוג, a small liquid measure
Sacred service vessels used in the מקדש
As long as / on condition that

phrases.english: or whether they do not hold a quarter-log;
phrases.notes: This is the end of a ברייתא. Its opening says a כהן may wash from any vessel, whether or not it holds a רביעית.

phrases.english: as long as they are service vessels!

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן רְבִיעִית; וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּהוּ כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא quoted before this section as a challenge to the rule that the כיור needs water for four כהנים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the כיור must hold enough water for four כהנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even a vessel holding less than a רביעית works, then the amount of water should not matter at all.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אחא: a small vessel set into a hole in the כיור
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אחא explains that the ברייתא is talking about a hole drilled in the כיור with a small vessel fixed in it. The small vessel is only a spout; the כיור itself still holds enough water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אחא said: It is talking about a case where one drills a hole in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אחא answers the challenge. He says the ברייתא means a small vessel attached to a hole in the כיור, so the water really comes from the big כיור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The small vessel can be tiny because it is only the opening that the water flows out of. The water comes from the כיור, which still holds enough for four כהנים. So the ברייתא and the size rule do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Drills or bores a hole
In it (in the כיור)

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Aḥa said:
It is where one drills a hole in it.
phrases.notes: He means a hole in the כיור with the small vessel fixed at the hole, so the water comes out through it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַחָא: בְּקוֹדֵחַ בְּתוֹכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means any separate small vessel can be used on its own.
steps.terutzMaskana: The small vessel is set into the כיור, and the כיור itself still holds water for four כהנים.

steps.title: The פסוק says to wash 'from it'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges using another vessel at all. The תורה says the כהנים wash 'from it,' meaning from the כיור itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the Merciful One said 'from it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on רב אדא בר אחא. The פסוק says the כהנים wash 'from it,' so how can they wash from a different vessel, even one attached to the כיור?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ממנו' seems to require that the washing be directly from the כיור. A separate vessel stuck into the כיור is still a different vessel. So the answer in step 2 seems to go against the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: From it
The Merciful One, a name for the תורה's Author
But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But the Merciful One said “from it”!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אדא בר אחא's answer in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אחא's case of a small vessel in the כיור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק requires washing 'from it,' from the כיור, not from another vessel.

steps.title: 'ירחצו' includes any כלי שרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the extra word 'ירחצו' in the next פסוק comes to include any כלי שרת, not only the כיור.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They shall wash' comes to include a service vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 3. Another word in the פסוקים, 'ירחצו,' widens the rule to include other כלי שרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ממנו' alone would limit washing to the כיור. But the extra word 'ירחצו' is read as a ריבוי, adding any כלי שרת. So a small sacred vessel can also be used.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall wash
To include, to widen the rule

phrases.english: “They shall wash” —
comes to include a service vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from 'ממנו' in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A second word in the פסוק widens the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ממנו' limits washing to the כיור alone.

steps.title: Then why not a כלי חול too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if 'ירחצו' widens the rule, maybe it should include even a כלי חול, an ordinary vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a non-sacred vessel too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 4. If 'ירחצו' adds other vessels, why stop at כלי שרת? Maybe even an ordinary vessel should work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ירחצו' does not mention sacred vessels. So once we use it to widen the rule, nothing seems to stop it from including a כלי חול. The גמרא wants to know what sets the limit.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
An ordinary, non-sacred vessel
Also, too

phrases.english: If so, a non-sacred vessel too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the ריבוי of 'ירחצו' in step 4 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: Limiting the ריבוי of 'ירחצו' to כלי שרת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing in the word 'ירחצו' limits it to sacred vessels, so it should include ordinary vessels too.

steps.title: אביי: a קל וחומר from the כיור's base rules out a כלי חול
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves that a כלי חול cannot be used. The base of the כיור was anointed together with it, and still a כהן may not wash from it. An ordinary vessel was never anointed, so surely it cannot be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You cannot say a non-sacred vessel, because of a קל וחומר from its base. Its base was anointed with it, and still it does not sanctify. A non-sacred vessel was not anointed with it, so surely it does not sanctify!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from step 5. He uses a קל וחומר from the כיור's base to show that a כלי חול is not included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The base of the כיור was anointed along with it (שמות 40:11), yet a כהן still cannot wash from water in the base. A כלי חול has less holiness, since it was never anointed. So if the base does not work, a כלי חול surely does not, and the ריבוי only covers כלי שרת.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
Its base (the stand of the כיור)
Was anointed (with the anointing oil)
Sanctifies; here, makes the washing of hands and feet valid
You cannot say

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן may wash from any כלי שרת that is set into the כיור, because 'ירחצו' includes it. אביי tries to rule out a כלי חול with a קל וחומר from the כיור's base. Step 9 knocks down this proof, and step 10 gives a different source.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
You cannot say a non-sacred vessel,
because of an a fortiori argument from its base;
phrases.notes: 'Its base' means the stand the כיור rested on.

phrases.english: and just as its base, which was anointed along with it —
does not sanctify;
a non-sacred vessel, which is not anointed along with it —
is it not logical that it does not sanctify?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כְּלִי חוֹל לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ, מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר מִכַּנּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5 by setting a limit on the ריבוי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ירחצו' might include even an ordinary vessel.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כלי חול is ruled out by a קל וחומר from the anointed base, which itself does not work.

steps.title: How do we know the base of the כיור is not valid for washing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source behind אביי's starting point, that a כהן may not wash from the כיור's base.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the base of the כיור, how do we know it is not valid for washing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask for a source for the fact that אביי built his proof on. It is setting up the next step, where a ברייתא gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's קל וחומר only works if we already know the base of the כיור is not valid for washing. Before relying on that, the גמרא wants to see where it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Its base, the stand the כיור rests on
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And its base, from where do we know?
phrases.notes: He means: how do we know the base of the כיור can't be used for washing, the fact אביי relied on in his proof?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the starting fact in אביי's קל וחומר
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source showing that the כן of the כיור cannot be used for washing

steps.title: The base matches the כיור only in being made of copper
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns from the פסוק that the base is linked to the כיור only for being made of copper. It is not linked to it for washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says, one might think the base can be used for washing just like the כיור. So the פסוק says, 'Make a copper כיור and its copper base.' The two are compared only for being made of copper, not for anything else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא of רבי יהודה. The פסוק joins the base to the כיור only for the material they are made of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק mentions the base together with the כיור, we might think the base works like the כיור in every way. רבי יהודה reads the shared word 'נחשת' as limiting the comparison to the copper only. So washing from the base is not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes holy, here meaning used for washing the hands and feet
Copper
I compared it (I linked them together)

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One might think its base should sanctify
phrases.notes: 'Sanctify' here means the כהן could wash his hands and feet from it.

phrases.english: just as the Basin sanctifies?
The verse states:
"You shall make a Basin of copper and its base of copper"
For copper I compared it
and not for any other matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question with a ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק compares the כן to the כיור only for being made of copper, so the כן is not valid for washing

steps.title: מר זוטרא breaks אביי's קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא points out that the base was never made to hold anything inside it, while a כלי חול is. So we cannot learn the כלי חול from the base.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא, son of רב מרי, said to רבינא: Why is the base not valid? Because it was not made to hold things inside it. Can you say the same about a כלי חול, which is made to hold things inside it?
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא attacks אביי's proof from step 6. He shows that the base has its own reason for not being valid, a reason that does not apply to an ordinary vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי argued that if even the anointed base is not valid, then surely an unanointed כלי חול is not valid. מר זוטרא says the base fails for a different reason: it is only a stand, not a container. A כלי חול really is a container, so the קל וחומר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: What about... (opens a reason why one case is different from another)
Made to hold things inside it, a real container
An ordinary vessel that is not holy

steps.confusionAlert: מר זוטרא is not saying a כלי חול is valid. He agrees it is not valid. He is only saying that אביי's proof does not work, so we need a different source.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Mari, said to Ravina:
What about its base? It is not made for its inside;
phrases.notes: The base is just a stand. It was never meant to hold water inside it.

phrases.english: Will you say so about a non-sacred vessel, which is made for its inside?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the קל וחומר of step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's קל וחומר from the כן to a כלי חול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כן is unfit because it is not a container, a weakness a כלי חול does not share, so the comparison breaks

steps.title: 'ממנו' is the source for excluding a כלי חול
steps.stepSummary: Since the קל וחומר failed, the גמרא uses the word 'ממנו' (from it) to exclude a כלי חול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the word 'from it' comes to exclude a כלי חול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces אביי's broken proof with a source from the פסוק. The word 'ממנו' is what rules out an ordinary vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3, 'ממנו' seemed to rule out every vessel other than the כיור. Now the גמרא gives it a narrower job: it excludes only a כלי חול. The result is the same as אביי's, but the reason is new.

keyTerms.meaning: From it, a word in the פסוק about washing from the כיור
To exclude

phrases.english: Rather, "from it" comes to exclude a non-sacred vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a new source after the קל וחומר was refuted
steps.terutzResolutionType: New scriptural source replacing a refuted logical proof
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כלי חול is excluded through אביי's קל וחומר from the כן
steps.terutzMaskana: A כלי חול is excluded through the word 'ממנו'

steps.title: Then 'ממנו' should exclude a כלי שרת too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if 'ממנו' excludes other vessels, it should also exclude a כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a כלי שרת should also be excluded!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the new reading of 'ממנו'. Plainly, 'from it' would rule out every vessel except the כיור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From it' sounds like 'only from the כיור.' So why should it exclude only an ordinary vessel and not a holy one too?

keyTerms.meaning: If so
A holy vessel used for the Temple service

phrases.english: If so, a service vessel too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the scope of 'ממנו' as set in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: Limiting the exclusion of 'ממנו' to a כלי חול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read plainly, 'ממנו' excludes everything except the כיור, including a כלי שרת

steps.title: 'ירחצו' includes a כלי שרת
steps.stepSummary: The תורה added the word 'ירחצו' to include a כלי שרת, so 'ממנו' cannot exclude it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תורה included more with the word 'they shall wash.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by going back to the extra word 'ירחצו' from step 4, which brings in a כלי שרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two words pulling in opposite directions. 'ירחצו' includes, and 'ממנו' excludes. Together they give the full picture: a כלי שרת is valid and a כלי חול is not.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה included (literally, the Merciful One made more)
They shall wash

phrases.english: But the Merciful One included with "they shall wash."
phrases.notes: This is the extra word from step 4, which brings in any כלי שרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by pointing to the including word
steps.terutzResolutionType: One word includes and another excludes, so each covers a different vessel
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ממנו' excludes all vessels, even a כלי שרת
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ירחצו' includes a כלי שרת, so 'ממנו' is left to exclude only a כלי חול

steps.title: Why include the כלי שרת and not the כלי חול?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we split the two words this way, instead of the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see that made you decide this way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why 'ירחצו' goes to the כלי שרת and 'ממנו' goes to the כלי חול. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one word that includes and one that excludes, either vessel could have been placed on either side. The גמרא wants a reason for the split it chose.

keyTerms.meaning: And what did you see? (why choose this way and not the reverse)

phrases.english: And what did you see?
phrases.notes: He means: why include the holy vessel and exclude the ordinary one, and not the other way around?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the way the two words were divided between the two vessels
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A reason for giving the inclusion to the כלי שרת and the exclusion to the כלי חול

steps.title: A כלי שרת needs anointing like the כיור
steps.stepSummary: A כלי שרת is like the כיור because both needed anointing. A כלי חול did not, so it is the one excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one (a כלי שרת) needs anointing like the כיור, and that one (a כלי חול) does not need anointing like it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the כלי שרת is more like the כיור, so it is the one included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כיור was anointed with oil, and so were the כלי שרת. A כלי חול never was. Since the כלי שרת shares this feature with the כיור, it makes sense to include it and leave out the ordinary vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: Needs anointing with oil
Like it, meaning like the כיור

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן may wash from the כיור or from any כלי שרת ('ירחצו'), but not from a כלי חול ('ממנו'). The holy vessel wins because it was anointed like the כיור.

phrases.english: This one requires anointing like it,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the כלי שרת, and 'like it' means like the כיור.

phrases.english: and that one does not require anointing like it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why the inclusion goes to the כלי שרת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כלי שרת is like the כיור in needing anointing, so it is the one included, and the unanointed כלי חול is excluded

steps.title: What completes a מקוה also completes the כיור, but not a רביעית
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that anything that may complete a מקוה may complete the כיור, but not a רביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says: Anything that may fill up the missing amount of a מקוה may also fill up the missing amount of the כיור. But it may not fill up a רביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a new rule comparing three kinds of water: the מקוה, the כיור, and the small רביעית used for washing hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כיור is treated like a מקוה. Water that is short of the full amount may be topped off with whatever is allowed for a מקוה. A רביעית is stricter, and that same topping-off does not work there.

keyTerms.meaning: Completes, meaning it tops off a missing amount
A ritual bath, which needs a set amount of water
The Basin in the מקדש that the כהנים washed from
A quarter-לוג, the amount of water needed for washing hands

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says:
Anything that completes the water of a ritual bath
completes the water of the Basin.
For a quarter-log, it does not complete.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the כיור after the earlier discussion of which vessels are excluded.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whatever may complete a מקוה may complete the כיור, but it may not complete a רביעית.

steps.title: What does ריש לקיש come to exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which item is allowed for a מקוה but not allowed for a רביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this rule meant to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the next few steps. It wants to know which actual case fits ריש לקיש's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's rule only matters if some item can complete a מקוה but cannot complete a רביעית. The גמרא is looking for that item.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude what?

phrases.english: To exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which case ריש לקיש's rule is about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which item may complete a מקוה but may not complete a רביעית?

steps.title: It cannot be liquefied mud
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests liquefied mud and rejects it with a cow test that treats the מקוה and the רביעית the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it excludes thin, watery mud, what exactly is the case? If it is thin enough that a cow can bend down and drink from it, then it should count even for a רביעית. If a cow cannot drink from it, then it should not count even for a מקוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that ריש לקיש means טיט הנדוק, watery mud. It then shows that this cannot be his case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cow test decides whether mud counts as water at all. If it counts as water, it works everywhere. If it does not, it works nowhere. So mud cannot be the case that works for a מקוה but not for a רביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offers a suggestion that may be rejected)
Thin, watery mud
What is the case? How does it look?
Bends down and drinks

phrases.english: If you say: to exclude liquefied mud
what is the case?
If a cow can bend down and drink from it,
then even for a quarter-log too!
phrases.notes: A cow drinking from it shows it still counts as water.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אֵין פָּרָה שׁוֹחָה וְשׁוֹתָה מִמֶּנּוּ,
phrases.english: And if a cow cannot bend down and drink from it,
then even for a ritual bath it does not complete!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question and knocks it down.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects liquefied mud as the excluded case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The cow test either allows mud for both the מקוה and the רביעית, or for neither. It never splits them.

steps.title: It cannot be red gnats either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests red gnats and rejects them, because things that come from water are kosher for a מקוה even by themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe it excludes red gnats? But those would count even on their own! As we learned in a ברייתא, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that you may immerse in anything that was first created from water. And רב יצחק בר אבדימי says you may even immerse in a fish's eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a second suggestion, יבחושין אדומין (red gnats). It rejects this one too, using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש is talking about something that only helps complete a מקוה. Red gnats come from water, and things that come from water count as water completely. You could immerse in them even on their own, so they are not a 'completing-only' item.

keyTerms.meaning: Red gnats, tiny creatures that grow in water
By themselves, on their own
Where it was first created
We immerse

phrases.english: Rather, to exclude red gnats
Even on their own too!
phrases.notes: He means that red gnats could make up the whole מקוה by themselves, not only top it off.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Anything whose creation began from the water
one may immerse in it;
And Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi says:
One may immerse in the eye of a fish!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mud failed, so the גמרא tries a second answer and rejects it too.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects red gnats as the excluded case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Things created from water count fully as water, so they are more than a completing-only item.

steps.title: רב פפא: it excludes adding a סאה and removing a סאה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says ריש לקיש excludes the case of adding one סאה of other liquid and then removing one סאה, which works for a מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: It excludes the case where someone put in a סאה and took out a סאה. As we learned in a משנה: A מקוה has exactly forty סאה of water. Someone put in one סאה of another liquid and then took out one סאה. The מקוה is still kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the real answer to the question 'what does it exclude?'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full מקוה can absorb a סאה of other liquid. After a סאה is taken out, the מקוה still counts as having forty סאה, so the added liquid has 'completed' it. For a רביעית this trick does not work, and that is the case ריש לקיש excludes.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of volume; a מקוה needs forty of them
He put in a סאה and took out a סאה
Exactly, no more and no less

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the whole difference between a מקוה and a רביעית in ריש לקיש's rule.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
To exclude: he put in a se'a and took out a se'a.
As we learned in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: מִקְוֶה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה מְכוָּּונוֹת;
phrases.english: A ritual bath that has exactly forty se'a;
he put in a se'a and took out a se'a
phrases.notes: The סאה he put in is some other liquid, not water.

phrases.english: it is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לְמַעוֹטֵי נָתַן סְאָה וְנָטַל סְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Two suggestions were rejected, so רב פפא gives a working answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The excluded case is adding a סאה of other liquid and removing a סאה. This works for a מקוה and the כיור, but not for a רביעית.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: this works up to most of the מקוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limits the 'add a סאה, remove a סאה' rule: it works only up to the majority of the מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה בר שילא said in the name of רב אסי, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This works up until most of the מקוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the משנה that רב פפא quoted, in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may keep adding and removing a סאה at a time, but only up to the majority of the מקוה. This limit finishes the picture of the case ריש לקיש was talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: Up to its majority

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש means: the 'add a סאה, remove a סאה' method works for a מקוה (up to most of it) and for the כיור, but never for a רביעית for washing hands.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda bar Sheila says

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that Rav Asi says that Rabbi Yochanan says:
Up to its majority.
phrases.notes: He means you can repeat this until most of the מקוה has been switched, but not beyond that.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the משנה that רב פפא brought.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'add a סאה, remove a סאה' method works only up to the majority of the מקוה.

steps.title: A small hole in the wall of a מקוה can be used for immersion
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that if someone drilled a hole in the wall of a מקוה that holds a רביעית, small items like needles and hooks may be immersed in it, because its water gets its fitness from the מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: If someone drilled a hole in the wall of a מקוה that holds a רביעית, you may immerse needles and hooks in it, because its water gets its fitness from the מקוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a new ruling about a small hole cut into the side of a מקוה. Even though the hole is a separate little space, small items may be immersed in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, a רביעית of water could never act as a מקוה. Here, though, the water in the hole is connected to the מקוה and comes from it, so it shares the מקוה's fitness. Needles and hooks are small enough to fit inside a רביעית-sized hole.

keyTerms.meaning: drilled, bored a hole
a quarter-לוג, a small measure of liquid
we immerse (to make an item טהור)
needles and hooks, very small metal items
the fitness of the מקוה

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
If one drilled in it a hole holding a quarter-log,
phrases.notes: "In it" means in the wall of the מקוה.

phrases.english: one may immerse needles and hooks in it,
since it comes from the fitness of the ritual bath.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אִם קָדַח בּוֹ רְבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel to רב אדא בר אחא's case of drilling into the כיור (step 2). Water in a drilled hole draws its fitness from the main body of water, here applied to a מקוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A רביעית-sized hole in a מקוה wall may be used to immerse small vessels, because its water draws its fitness from the מקוה.

steps.title: מקוה water may be used for the כיור
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes ריש לקיש: water of a מקוה is fit to be used as water of the כיור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה says in the name of ריש לקיש: Water of a מקוה is fit to be used as water for the כיור.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling is stated: מקוה water is kosher for the כיור, the Basin the כהנים wash from. This ruling sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מקוה can be filled with gathered rainwater, which is not spring water. So this ruling suggests that the כיור does not need spring water.

keyTerms.meaning: water of a ritual bath (can be gathered rainwater)
the Basin in the מקדש from which the כהנים washed hands and feet
fit, valid

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya says that Reish Lakish says:
Water of a ritual bath is fit to be used as water of the Basin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: מֵי מִקְוֶה כְּשֵׁירִים לְמֵי כִיּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement about which water is fit for the כיור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מקוה water is valid for use in the כיור.

steps.title: Challenge: a ברייתא suggests כיור water is מים חיים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether this means כיור water need not be מים חיים. A ברייתא learns from 'with water' that other waters are fit for washing the innards, and adds that כיור water is fit by a קל וחומר. That קל וחומר seems to be based on כיור water being מים חיים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean כיור water does not have to be flowing water? But a ברייתא teaches: 'With water' means not with wine. 'With water' means not with diluted wine. 'With water' comes to include other waters. And כיור water is included by a קל וחומר. What is the קל וחומר for כיור water? Isn't it that it is flowing water?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's ruling. It uses a ברייתא that seems to assume כיור water is spring water, which is better than מקוה water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says even ordinary water may be used to wash the innards of a קרבן, and כיור water all the more so. A קל וחומר needs some special quality in כיור water. The obvious quality is that it is מים חיים. If that is right, rainwater from a מקוה should not be fit for the כיור.

keyTerms.meaning: flowing, living water (spring water)
wine diluted with water
other kinds of water
a logical 'all the more so' argument

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is about washing the innards of a קרבן, not about filling the כיור. The גמרא only uses its קל וחומר to learn what is special about כיור water.

phrases.english: Is this to say that Basin water need not be flowing water?!
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
"With water" and not with wine;
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:9, about washing the innards of a קרבן.

phrases.english: "with water" and not with diluted wine;
"with water" to include other types of water;
and all the more so the water of the Basin.
What is the 'all the more so' for Basin water?
Is it not because it is flowing water?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּלָא מַיִם חַיִּים נִינְהוּ? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's ruling from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling that מקוה water is fit for the כיור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's קל וחומר implies that כיור water is better than ordinary water, most likely because it is מים חיים. If so, מקוה rainwater should be invalid for the כיור.

steps.title: Answer: the special quality is that Basin water is sanctified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the קל וחומר is not based on spring water. It is based on the fact that כיור water is sanctified.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The קל וחומר is because כיור water is sanctified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש. It gives a different reason why כיור water is 'all the more so' fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The special quality of כיור water is its holiness from being in a sanctified vessel, not where it came from. So the ברייתא does not prove that the כיור needs spring water, and ריש לקיש's ruling survives.

keyTerms.meaning: because it is sanctified

phrases.english: No, it is because it is sanctified.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out; the meaning stays the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the basis of the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר assumed כיור water is spring water.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר is based on כיור water being sanctified, so spring water is not required.

steps.title: Challenge: is sanctified water really an advantage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether being sanctified makes water better. It cites the school of שמואל, who taught that 'water' in the פסוק means water with no added name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is being sanctified really an advantage? But the school of שמואל taught: 'Water' means water that has no added name...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It starts quoting a teaching that seems to point the other way, and the teaching continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה wants plain water with no extra label, then 'sanctified water' may count as water with an added name. That would make it worse, not better. The קל וחומר based on holiness then looks shaky.

keyTerms.meaning: an advantage, a better quality
the school of שמואל taught
an added name, a modifier attached to a word

phrases.english: And is being sanctified an advantage?
But didn't the school of Shmuel teach:
"Water" means water that has no added name,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַדִּישֵׁי מְעַלְּיוּתָא הִיא? וְהָא תָּנָא דְּבֵי שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that sanctified status makes כיור water better
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה's 'water' means plain water with no modifier. Water called 'sanctified water' may carry a modifier, so holiness would not be an advantage.
